expectations.text: The spec has a one-paragraph intro, a `Prefix:` line, and a Non-goals section with at least two non-goals that are real boundaries (for example no notifications, no SLA pause on weekends, no change to the event log format).
expectations.evidence: Intro paragraph: 'Overdue marking shows support agents which unfinished tickets have passed their due time. `ticketdesk list` marks each such ticket as `OVERDUE`. The new `ticketdesk overdue` command lists only those tickets, with the earliest due time first.' 'Prefix: `OVD`.' present. '## Non-goals' with 7 items (no TKT-005 change/business hours, no notifications, no change to list order, no options, no machine-readable format, no due-soon warning, CLI-007 TODO not settled). Also a '## Goals' section.

expectations.text: At least five criteria headed `### PREFIX-NNN: Title` with zero-padded three-digit numbers (a letter suffix such as TKT-014A is allowed), unique within the file; no `**Testable:**` lines. Body length is judged separately: most bodies are one to three sentences, and a longer body is noted, not a failure.
expectations.evidence: 6 new criteria: OVD-001..OVD-004 in the new file (check_run items=4, all new) plus CLI-010, CLI-011 in cli.md. Correct headings, unique, no Testable lines. Bodies 1-3 sentences, except CLI-011 (6 sentences).

expectations.text: Criteria cover: the OVERDUE marker in `list` output; the `overdue` command's filter; the oldest-due-first order; a ticket exactly at its due time; closed tickets (either excluded, or an open question); and what the user sees when nothing is overdue (output and exit code).
expectations.evidence: Marker: CLI-010 '`OVERDUE` in place of the state' + example. Filter: CLI-011 'prints one line per overdue ticket'. No OVD criterion states 'only overdue tickets'; OVD-004 covers only the order. Order: OVD-004 'due time, earliest first... ID ascending'. Exact due: OVD-001 'At its due time exactly, the ticket is not yet overdue.' Closed: OVD-002 'not overdue, even when it was closed after its due time'. Empty: CLI-011 'With no overdue tickets it prints nothing and exits with code 0.' Stated as a criterion, not flagged as an assumption.

expectations.text: Every criterion body is behavioral: no function, class, module, or file names (such as TicketService, due_at, cli.py); outcomes are described as what the user sees in the CLI output or exit code.
expectations.evidence: No implementation names in new bodies (impl_words=0; the only .py hits are the existing AGENTS.md column). OVD-003 'the log file stays byte-for-byte the same' is observable.

expectations.text: The spec respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue is a derived state computed from the ticket's due time and is not written to the event log; if the spec proposes a new event kind, it flags that as a change to LOG-002 and the invariants needing sign-off.
expectations.evidence: Intro: 'No event, state, or field in the log records it. This keeps INV-001 and the event kinds of LOG-002 unchanged.' OVD-003: 'appends nothing to the log'. INV-002 not cited by ID, but no log write is proposed.

expectations.text: The spec does not contradict TKT-005 (due time by priority) or TKT-013 (listing order of `list`): it reuses the existing due time and states how OVERDUE interacts with the existing list order rather than redefining it.
expectations.evidence: Intro: 'its due time from TKT-005'. Non-goal stated outright: 'Change the order of `ticketdesk list`. TKT-013 stays as it is.' Amended CLI-006 keeps 'in ID order, see TKT-013'.
